programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Celia Imrie explores the story behind Francis Ford Coppola’s acclaimed Godfather series. Through interviews and insights from leading cast members Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, James Caan, Robert Duvall and Coppola himself, we discover how this tale of family betrayal, shocking violence and a horse’s head in a bed resulted in two films that are widely considered amongst cinema’s greatest achievements of the 1970s – and how the third part of the trilogy, released 16 years after Godfather II, was a less happy experience, where one leading cast member was made an offer he could, and did, refuse.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Building of Britain
programme.desc: Fred Dibnah investigates one of the greatest feats of royal engineering - the construction of the great chain of castles on the coast of north Wales. Travelling to Harlech, Caernarfon and Beaumaris, Fred reveals the building techniques and revolutionary defensive features that helped Edward I subdue the rebellious Welsh. Fred also charts the achievements of the king's architect Master James of St Georges, a Frenchman who revolutionised castle design in England.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson unearths the unique past of Porthgain, a small Pembrokeshire village built for its industry, first as a slate quarry, then exporting brickwork and finally producing a granite-like stone that helped to create the nation’s roads. The heavy industrial infrastructure that remains in this tiny village is a sight to behold. Porthgain’s prosperity rose and fell over the years, and many of the houses were owned by the quarry companies who mined there. Eventually, the villagers took back control and bought the village themselves.

programme.title: Steve Backshall's Extreme Mountain Challenge
programme.desc: Adventurer and naturalist Steve Backshall embarks on one of the most dramatic and dangerous expeditions ever filmed by a BBC crew. His mission is to explore Venezuela's tepuis - ancient, sheer-sided mountains, lost worlds cut off from the jungle below. With an elite team of rock climbers, Steve attempts the first ascent of an unclimbed wall on a remote tepui to search for wildlife on the summit. But nobody could have predicted what would happen, nor the kinds of decisions they'd be forced to make. A white-knuckle ride from the start, the team encounter river rapids and hazardous wildlife, and survive a close shave with a rickety biplane. Yet nothing can prepare them for their climb to the island in the sky.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: In 1958, A Taste of Honey burst onto the British stage. Written by the teenage Sheila Delaney, it tackled taboos with an ease and a humour that made audiences sit up and take notice. Playing truant to see the film version in 1961, Peter Egan is perfectly placed to discuss this landmark of British theatre. He tells us what it is about the play that made it stand out and how he was cast in the 1984 BBC version - the director remembering Peter's working-class roots despite his constantly being asked to play ‘lords and poets and kings’. He discusses the background to the play, John Osborne opening the door to a new kind of drama with Look Back in Anger, and the huge influence the iconic director Joan Littlewood had on the piece. But mostly, he reminds us why the play remains so powerful and still has such relevance today.

programme.title: A Taste of Honey
programme.desc: 1984 adaptation of Shelagh Delaney's classic play.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Dame Sian Phillips looks back on Dylan Thomas’s Under Milk Wood and her own experiences with the various adaptions that have brought perhaps the world’s most celebrated ‘play for voices’ to cinema and television audiences. She recalls the BBC’s 2014 version that brought together a huge range of Welsh talent, including Tom Jones, Matthew Rhys, Charlotte Church, Michael Sheen and Katherine Jenkins. She also looks further back, sharing the story of her encounters with Dylan Thomas and her part in the 1972 film, which saw her working alongside the great Richard Burton, his wife Elizabeth Taylor and her then-husband Peter O’Toole.

programme.title: Under Milk Wood
programme.desc: A unique one-off television production of Dylan Thomas's famous 'play for voices' performed by a community of Welsh talent in New York, Los Angeles, London, Cardiff and Laugharne. Michael Sheen opens as First Voice with Sir Tom Jones as Captain Cat, and as each of Thomas's iconic characters joins in, the piece builds up into a collage of famous voices and faces (including Matthew Rhys, Ioan Gruffudd, Siân Phillips, Jonathan Pryce, Bryn Terfel and Katherine Jenkins) intercut with evocative imagery inspired by the play and created as part of a live event by National Theatre Wales.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Author and broadcaster Nigel Williams examines the work and the legend of one of the most famous poets of the 20th century, Dylan Thomas. Born in 1914, Dylan Thomas was an unruly and undisciplined child who was interested only in English at school and was determined from childhood to become a poet. Little did he know that he would eventually become world-renowned. Cited by Bob Dylan, John Lennon, Van Morrison and other cultural icons as a profound influence, Thomas occupies the space more readily associated with the likes of James Dean and Jack Kerouac, both of whom he preceded. But it was his death that truly made him a legend. Did Dylan Thomas really die after drinking 18 straight whiskies at The White Horse in New York? Was he a genius or a sponging, womanising drunk? The film unravels the myth by tracing the poet's biography backwards, from his much-written-about, much-lied-about death, to the heart of the Dylan Thomas story and his beginnings in a quiet street in suburban Swansea.

programme.title: Abandoned: Searching for Soldier Dad
programme.desc: DNA detectives track down the British soldiers who fathered children in Kenya then disappeared, leaving the children and their mothers without support. It's a quest to find a missing part of the children's identities. With access to every stage of this cutting-edge process, we follow as a team of lawyers and a leading geneticist travel to Kenya to help locate the British soldiers who fathered children then vanished. We witness the groundbreaking legal and scientific detective work used to find the missing dads. Lawyers believe British soldiers stationed at the army base in Nanyuki, Kenya, may have fathered hundreds of children over decades - the oldest we meet is now 70, the youngest just 18 months old. What's at stake is more than the reputation of the British army and the UK's post-colonial legacy. The mixed-heritage children have in some cases been ostracised by their communities and denied a chance of British citizenship since birth - something which could transform their lives.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: 'Meat proxy' is a new term coined to describe someone who acts as a human conduit for material generated by AI. Software engineer Niklas Gruhn, who came up with the phrase, joins Will Oremus of The Atlantic and Fortune’s Diane Brady to discuss how much AI is being used in journalism and when readers should be told about it. Five years after US troops withdrew from Afghanistan and the Taliban returned to power, Lyse Doucet has been back in the country, including visiting one of the secret schools set up for girls. BBC News’ Chief International Correspondent discusses what it takes to report from Afghanistan now, the restrictions she encountered and the difficult decisions involved in protecting contributors. A new series of The Grand Tour has three new presenters following the departure of Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May. This time, social media creators are taking over the long-running motoring show. Phil Churchward, its director and executive producer, explains how they were chosen.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: Eighty years ago, an icon of travel first appeared from a Tuscan assembly line - the Vespa. Qasa Alom takes to Tuscany's roads on a vintage scooter to explore a region whose reputation as a playground for the rich and famous also hides a fascinating blue-collared history. Qasa meets the last few working Tuscan cowboys of Maremma as they gather in their cattle and explain how tourism is now their bread and butter; and he heads to the caves of Carrara to see the dangers and hard work involved in mining some of the most-prized marble in the world.

programme.title: Talking Movies
programme.desc: To mark America's 250th anniversary, Talking Movies hears from leading figures in US media, film and culture who tell the BBC about some iconic American movies and what these films reveal about the country and the psyche of her people. American Psycho director Mary Harron talks about Martin Scorsese's The King of Comedy, while critic and film-maker Bilge Ebiri looks at Hitchcock's classic thriller North by Northwest. BBC News presenter Sumi Somaskanda reveals her passion for the prison drama The Shawshank Redemption and award-winning journalist Tim Teeman selects Steven Spielberg's Jaws. Talking Movies' host Tom Brook chooses the Robert Altman ensemble satire Nashville. Each contributor speaks about what their film choice means to them and how and why they feel it has become an American cinema classic. This special illustrates the American nation on the big screen and the influence it's had in bringing its movies to the world.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: China can build a robot that runs faster than Usain Bolt. So why can't it reliably empty a dishwasher? We explore the gap between what AI can think and what robots can actually do. As viral clips from Beijing's World Humanoid Robot Games showcase astonishing feats and spectacular failures, we ask whether China is leading a robotics revolution or exposing the limits of today's technology. Christian Fraser and Priya Lakhani are joined by Oxford Robotics Institute founder Professor Ingmar Posner and Laelaps AI co-founder Maria Stamatopoulou to examine why building a robot body is getting easier, but building a robot mind remains one of AI's greatest challenges.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Julia Somerville, Louise Minchin and Gloria Hunniford hear from the passengers whose flight hit a storm so severe they feared for their lives. The airline said it was fine to fly, but the passengers disagree. Also on the programme, the holidaymakers who have lost thousands of pounds to scam villa rentals. The team reveal how you can spot the increasingly convincing but totally bogus websites. And the caravan owner who is asking for help after her van's window developed mysterious cracks.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion feels like he has a mountain to climb in Blackpool... at a mid-terrace with potential subsidence! He’s also in Leicester, grappling with a non-standard construction property. Martin’s in Somerset to meet a mother-and-daughter team on a mission to create a dream home.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: With more than a hundred miles of canals, Warwickshire’s waterways are a kaleidoscope of colour. Canal art adorns many of the county’s narrowboats, bringing vivid splashes of greens, reds and yellows to its towpaths. Presenter Caroline Hawley meets heritage crafter Kerri Williams, who specialises in preserving this traditional art form. Kerri runs workshops teaching the art and helping students to understand the social history behind it. In nearby Long Marston, two generations of antiques hunters search high and low for bargains to take to auction. In red are mum and daughter Bekki and Paisley, and in blue are mum and son Francine and Richard. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds’ tails are wagging when they spot a vintage ceramic bulldog that is identical to one in a well-known spy movie. However, when expert David Fergus sees the price tag, he says they’re barking up the wrong tree. Meanwhile, the blue team and their expert, Thomas Forrester, find a soapstone sculpture of a lion, but sadly its condition is far from 'purrfect'. In Bristol, the bidders are in a generous mood when auctioneer Andy Stowe starts selling the teams’ lots – but who’s going home with cash in their hands?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Sister Boniface Mysteries
programme.desc: Arthur Salem is found in a locked room, stabbed in the back with a knife held in the hand of his newest doll. His employees are the prime suspects. Sister Boniface investigates.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Denise Nurse is in Nottinghamshire, helping Canadian house hunter Shane swap London life for the countryside. He is bringing his two cats but dreams of a garden big enough for a couple of dogs, too. The property search includes a brilliant three-for-one mystery house with not one but two annexes. Denise also heads to Sherwood Forest to discover how climate change is affecting its ancient oak trees and learns about what is being done to protect them.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie is in Fareham, Hampshire to revisit the garden of Vanessa and Alan. Seven years ago, the couple wanted a grand Italian garden which would turn into one of the team's toughest assignments. Years later, the showstopping Mediterranean wonder looks more amazing than ever with stunning olive trees, old stone walls and a giant Scots pine. Charlie discovers not only a changed garden but a changed family. We also revisit the Leicester garden where the team bought a bit of country to suburbia and a tiny plot in Shefford that became a stunning multi-functional garden.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts the exciting, fast-paced general knowledge quiz show where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions hurtling down the Answer Run towards them. St Giles’ Cathedral has been a working church for over 900 years, serving as the backdrop to Scotland’s religious history. The cathedral has been at the centre of the Scottish Reformation, from its inception in 1124 as a Romanesque church to its current standing as a modern Presbyterian place of worship. Dane's lifelong best friend Stefan and girlfriend Nicola both try to help Dane keep his cool, but he is soon under the influence of Dad's birthday rum and expressing things that might be better left unsaid, much to the enjoyment of Christian and his twin sister Kadean.

programme.title: Sunny D
programme.desc: With Dane finding himself engaged, the pressure is on for him to leave the parental home and start a new life with Nicola. Dane will need to save a fortune if he is ever going to find a habitable place to rent, but his office life is getting worse and worse thanks to his new boss, the ferocious, flirtatious Kerry. When Nicola catches him in a compromising position with Kerry, she is furious at his lack of courage and arranges a night of revenge by heading out on the town with her two flatmates and Kadean. Dane is left to fantasise about worst-case scenarios, both at home and in the office, as his life goes from bad to worse.

programme.title: Sunny D
programme.desc: Having made Dane suffer, Nicola agrees to carry on with their engagement, and plans are made for a wedding meeting, where Dane's parents will be introduced to Jamaar, Nicola's dad. Jamaar is a part-time/failed DJ and a part-time/failed Dad who has only been back in touch with Nicola since she has found financial security. Dane arrives at the meeting having had a disastrous day at work - humiliated by Kerry at an interdepartment football match. Jamaar goes out of his way to wind up Dane until he eventually explodes. The consequences would be even more disastrous if it weren't for the fact that Kadean has an even more explosive announcement.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: An 'ancient' pyramid appears overnight. Every clock in the world begins counting down to the Earth's destruction. Three opposing armies lie ready to annihilate each other. An alien race stands ready to offer humanity a deal that could save them, but also enslave them. It's a terrifying race against time to save the world. Will the Doctor be forced to accept their help?

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Nicola gets a shock when the Hawkinses arrive in Walford. Wedding fever sweeps Walford ahead of Cindy and Kim’s big days. And Priya wrestles with her guilt.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: The Hawkinses make their presence known in Albert Square. Ravi pushes Priya for information about what happened whilst he was away.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Nicola has a change of heart and offers an olive branch. Ravi’s suspicions make him determined to find the truth. A power cut threatens Linda’s event at the community centre.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: The men of Walford gather in Harry’s Barn for Max and Howie’s stag party. Linda is forced to decide between her head and her heart. And Max attempts to talk his way out of a situation, but will it be enough?

programme.title: Creed
programme.desc: Itching to refine his raw talent, young boxer Adonis seeks help from reluctant Rocky Balboa, opponent and friend of the illegitimate lad’s late father, Apollo Creed.

programme.title: Creed II
programme.desc: Adonis, whose trainer is Rocky Balboa, is challenged to fight Viktor Drago, son of the man who killed Apollo Creed. A most unequal contest.

programme.title: Vigil
programme.desc: After the murder of a British citizen in the Arctic, DCI Amy Silva and DI Kirsten Longacre investigate. As Amy looks into a possible conspiracy on Scottish soil, Kirsten comes up against uncooperative Russian inhabitants, who are claiming foul play and obstructing her at every turn. But then they discover a missing person who could set a match to this political tinderbox.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Diarmuid Gavin are in Powys to help mum and daughter Kim and Ashleigh tackle their uninspired garden, where a bramble-choked bank hides an apple tree and butterfly bushes. Their dream? To turn the wilderness from bramble bank to bounty, provided by a vibrant veggie haven. After three years of sharing a home and making it their own, the garden has been left behind. Now, they want to transform the overgrown slope into a productive, low-maintenance space filled with colourful plants and homegrown vegetables. With no grass to worry about, it needs to be easy to access and safe for their beloved dog. For Kim and Ashleigh, a beautiful, practical garden would not only complement the stunning landscape beyond their plot but also provide a peaceful retreat to boost their mental well-being. Can the team turn brambles into bounty on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: With three skip finds secured, upcycler Jacqui Joseph is on a mission to turn unloved items into must-have interiors. Furniture artist Chloe is tasked with saving a tired headboard and new maker Jacob's under pressure to strike the right chord with a guitar-themed table. Will Jacqui be 'amped up' when she sees it?

programme.title: A House Through Time
programme.desc: During the first two decades of the 20th century, life for many in Edinburgh is hard. The demolition of the slums in the Old Town has put pressure on living spaces, and the house on Calton Hill has been subdivided to accommodate more families. Featured are the Marshalls, a family of five occupying just two rooms and sharing the floor and toilet with another household; the Ross family, including head prison warder James, who is brutally attacked by an inmate; and Annie Anthony and her son John, a professional soldier who fought a very different sort of war.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Rickie Haywood-Williams, Sally Phillips, Vikki Stone and Dan Walker take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the House of Games golden goblets, or will they be tempted by the branded golden fondue set?

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: Gabby Logan takes charge of the quiz where contestants need brainpower and ball skills to win big. Who will be the high roller and who will push themselves over The Edge?

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: 'Derek the Weatherman’ hopes it will be warm when he takes part in the World Bog Snorkelling championships in mid Wales. It’s at the end of his walk that follows part of the trail along the Heart of Wales Railway, starting in Llandovery. On his way, he takes part in a tug-of-war with young farmers and has afternoon tea under an impressive railway viaduct. Matthew Bassett joins cyclists in Llandovery, and wildlife expert Lizzie Daly goes in search of pied flycatchers in rare Atlantic oak woodland.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Ben and Kate return to Longleat where hopes are rising for the first baby southern koala in Europe.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! is at the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. Antiques experts Michael Baggott and Anita Manning find some real gems among the bags and boxes to take to auction, including a fascinating pair of beaded gloves and an amber necklace that takes the saleroom by storm. Paul Martin explores the history of one of London's premier art schools and visits one of Britain's few remaining Palladian houses.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Ken Bruce, Alice Roberts, Perri Shakes-Drayton and Kiell Smith-Bynoe take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour of the green and pleasant landscape between the North and South Downs, known as the Weald, nears its conclusion.

programme.title: Iolo's Anglesey
programme.desc: Iolo Williams explores the wildlife of Anglesey. Wales’s largest island is renowned for its coastal beauty, and also for the spectacular wildlife that can be found in its sand dunes, rocky cliffs and surrounding farmland. Iolo finds colourful day-flying moths, beautiful orchids and brown hares. He heads out to the Skerries Islands and visits Wales’s only Arctic tern colony. Along the way, he also encounters a fox and comes across a small owl with its chick on an abandoned farm near Holyhead.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: With the days getting shorter, and the nights cooler, George Anderson and Calum Clunie review some of the Beechgrove planting projects they started in the spring. A new addition was Calum’s family plot, based on the standard garden size of a new build property, and Calum returns to harvest and assess just how productive the area has been. George and Calum are in the trials bed to compare how the various club root-resistant varieties of brassica have performed after the infection was found in this area of the garden. The pair also visit the grass garden that was completely overhauled and replanted at the start of the series. There are visits to Jenna McDonald at her allotment in Perth and Colin Crosbie’s plot just outside Dumfries, and there are all the usual weekly handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty celebrates a rewarding summer fruit harvest, proving that careful cultivation can triumph even in severe drought conditions. He gathers baskets of ripe produce while looking ahead to autumn, planning and sowing crops to keep the kitchen supplied in the months to come. Along the way, he shares practical advice on reviving plants scorched by intense heat and begins an exciting renovation project that promises to bring fresh life and new possibilities to the garden. Carol Klein delves into the secret world of leaves to uncover the cutting-edge science and surprising new discoveries that are transforming our understanding of plant life. Rachel de Thame visits a head gardener in Hertfordshire who guides her around an extraordinary plant library packed with interesting specimens, while in Suffolk, there's a garden designer and passionate wildlife advocate whose garden has been carefully shaped to support both family life and biodiversity. Plus a visit to a dedicated houseplant grower in Edinburgh, who showcases an impressive collection and shares the enthusiasm that led to the creation of a thriving indoor jungle.

programme.title: The Marlow Murder Club
programme.desc: With the revelation that there’s going to be another murder, the team are in a race against time to stop the killer. Realising that their skills could help solve the case, Tanika goes out on a limb, bringing Judith, Becks and Suzie into the police investigation as civilian advisers. They uncover an important connection between the murders, but can they stop the killer before they strike again?

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Hannah takes a look at the air fryer – a device that is rapidly taking over people's kitchens, cooking up everything from bread rolls to baked Alaska and almost making ovens obsolete. Hannah dives into its surprising history, going behind the scenes with air fryer originators Philips. She discovers how the accidental creation of a wonder wire in the 1900s, a WWII pilot’s cold dinner and one man tinkering in his garage created this modern marvel that is redefining cooking.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Harvest
programme.desc: A remote rural village with no name is thrown into turmoil over the course of a hallucinatory few days.

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: The five remaining pairs continue their mission to become art dealers in the highly competitive art world as the pressure ramps up. They explore the world of prints and limited editions in Margate, the traditional seaside town that’s been transformed into a vibrant art destination. With over 30 galleries and artist studios, as well as the Turner Contemporary Gallery, which attracts over a quarter of a million visitors a year, it’s the perfect place to test the dealers’ ability to sell directly to the public. Steph and series mentor Cordelia de Freitas are joined by artist and Margate gallery owner, Margo McDaid - someone who knows the value of the local print and limited-edition market.

programme.title: Vigil
programme.desc: After the kidnap of a government minister, Amy starts connecting the dots between his policy and his abduction as she zeroes in on the kidnapper. Kirsten navigates international agendas in the Arctic in the hunt for a missing Chinese scientist. Faced with an opportunity that could help her solve the case, Kirsten must risk consequences she may not be able to come back from.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: After the Piri theatre collapses, Brinicle tries to write a hit fundraising single to restore it but is stumped for ideas - until inspiration strikes in the unlikeliest of places.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: When Big Lizard and Cosima get covered in nectar, they become unwilling house guests to some overfriendly beetles. Will Dunk come to their rescue?

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings play pirates, taking turns to be the captain. They are over the moon when Weasy joins in the fun - until he breaks the rules of the game. There's only one solution: mutiny!

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The heroes are excited to visit Whizzpop’s Pop-Up Bakery and taste his magical cakes, but they are shocked to find that the protein bars have shouty raisins in them, the custard tarts are rock hard, and the floating sponges keep floating away! Trevor quests to solve the mystery, but having accidentally fallen into Whizzpop’s invisibility flour, how on earth will he get everyone’s attention?

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings find a jewel that gives them total control over the fireflies.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: When Duck and Frog get a job in a restaurant kitchen, Frog accidentally makes the soup incredibly spicy. He wants to serve it to a celebrity chef, but Duck wants to stop him!

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Tinkatuff goes on a quest to find the perfect metal for completing its hammer.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: When Vexius launches a devastating attack on Red Fountain, Winx and Specialists must unite to protect the school. Meanwhile, Bloom uncovers a shocking connection between Vexius and her Dragon Flame.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: High Hoops
programme.desc: Can new girl Aoife turn her school's rubbish basketball team into winners and make herself popular and cool at the same time?

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty celebrates a rewarding summer fruit harvest, proving that careful cultivation can triumph even in severe drought conditions. He gathers baskets of ripe produce while looking ahead to autumn, planning and sowing crops to keep the kitchen supplied in the months to come. Along the way, he shares practical advice on reviving plants scorched by intense heat and begins an exciting renovation project that promises to bring fresh life and new possibilities to the garden. Carol Klein delves into the secret world of leaves to uncover the cutting-edge science and surprising new discoveries that are transforming our understanding of plant life. Rachel de Thame visits a head gardener in Hertfordshire who guides her around an extraordinary plant library packed with interesting specimens, while in Suffolk, there's a garden designer and passionate wildlife advocate whose garden has been carefully shaped to support both family life and biodiversity. Plus a visit to a dedicated houseplant grower in Edinburgh, who showcases an impressive collection and shares the enthusiasm that led to the creation of a thriving indoor jungle.

programme.title: This Wild Life
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Saba Douglas-Hamilton, together with her husband Frank and their three young children, moves to the romantic Samburu National Reserve in Kenya to run a safari camp for the first time. But life out there isn't easy. There are monkeys in the kitchen, floods threatening the camp and, with no fences to keep out the wildlife, elephants are regular house guests. This series follows their ups and downs as the family struggles to keep guests, elephants, lions and even crocodiles smiling. Saba, Frank and the children have settled in to their new home at the safari camp, but life in this frontier gets tough as the summer heats up. Saba's guests are accidentally stranded at a remote airstrip in the scorching African sun. The team races to pick them up while Saba makes sure that the camp is ready. Husband Frank puts himself on the frontline in the fight against ivory poachers.

programme.title: G.I. Blues
programme.desc: Tulsa, a soldier with dreams of running his own nightclub, places a bet with his friend Dynamite that he can win the heart of an untouchable dancer. But when Dynamite is transferred, Tulsa must replace him in the bet.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's week 8, and the five remaining sewers must channel their inner bookworm in a series of challenges celebrating literary icons. For the Pattern Challenge, the judges ask the sewers to create literature’s most iconic piece of headwear, the deerstalker worn by Arthur Conan Doyle’s character Sherlock Holmes. It's a challenge that at this stage of the competition is far from elementary. In the Transformation Challenge, they must imagine what the iconic children’s character Matilda would be like as a grown-up and create an outfit for her from second-hand school uniform. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, everyone must travel back to the turn of the 19th century and the Regency period by creating outfits inspired by the works of Jane Austen.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles and the teams go shopping for antiques in West Sussex with experts Kate Bliss and Gary Pe. Eric also visits artist Rosi Robinson to learn about the ancient craft of batik. As usual, there are highs and lows at the auction, but which team will reign supreme?

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: The remaining teams return to St Andrews Beach for an ocean-inspired challenge. From dolphins and sea monsters to Poseidon himself, they have just six hours to sculpt marine masterpieces before the tide sweeps in. Judges Sadie and Jamie demand killer concepts, technical skill and movement, but disaster strikes when Alex and Remy’s towering Poseidon collapses. Can they salvage their design? As the waves close in, Mary and Paul frantically work on their dynamic dolphin sculpture, while Helen and Martin hope their kelpie will impress the judges. Who will sink and who will swim in this high-stakes race against nature?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Somerset is the destination today, where Alistair Appleton is helping an industrious young couple from Hertfordshire who are eager to make a rural move to the county.

programme.title: Rugby League: Super League
programme.desc: Action from the Super League as Wakefield Trinity take on Warrington Wolves.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Antiques experts Mark Stacey and Elizabeth Talbot join Paul Martin at Stapleford Park in the heart of the Leicestershire countryside, where Elizabeth spies a German set of doll's house furniture, and Mark falls for a set of Minton sporting tiles. Paul takes time out to explore nearby Kirby Hall, and discovers how this impressive building was designed for Queen Elizabeth I.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Much-loved magical tunes from Aladdin, Beauty and the Beast, The Little Mermaid and more, brought to life by singers Marisha Wallace, Lucie Jones and other West End stars. Be transported to A Whole New World with soaring ballads like Colors of the Wind and Part of Your World, as well as the show-stopping numbers Be Our Guest, Friend Like Me and Zero to Hero. Sarah Hicks conducts the BBC Philharmonic, and the concert features the National Youth Music Theatre. Presented by Nick Mohammed from the Royal Albert Hall.

programme.title: Athletics: Diamond League
programme.desc: Coverage from the 2026 Diamond League meeting in Brussels, Belgium.

programme.title: Queen at the BBC
programme.desc: A trip through the archives that serves up an hour of killer Queen material, featuring some of the band's greatest musical moments ever delivered to our screens. The legendary band’s huge international status and punishing touring schedules meant that over the years they made surprisingly few appearances on programmes like Top of the Pops, and tragically for their fans, several of those performances were either lost or never recorded. This collection brings together the very best of what’s survived from one of the most enduring and best-loved acts in British rock, featuring perhaps the most charismatic and popular frontman of all time. Amongst the gems are moments from the band’s celebrated 1975 concert at London’s Hammersmith Odeon and highlights from their trips to the prestigious Montreux Pop Festival in the 1980s – an event that attracted the cream of the world’s music acts every year. Songs featured take us from the band’s first-ever UK hit, Seven Seas of Rhye, through to These Are The Days of Our Lives, Queen’s last hit before Freddie’s untimely death, as well as all the biggest hits, including the iconic Bohemian Rhapsody.

programme.title: Queen: The Legendary 1975 Concert
programme.desc: On Christmas Eve 1975, Queen crowned a glorious year with a special concert at London's Hammersmith Odeon. The show on the final night of their triumphant UK tour was broadcast live on BBC TV and radio, and it has become a legendary event in Queen's history. Featuring stunning renditions of early hits Keep Yourself Alive, Liar and Now I'm Here alongside Brian May's epic guitar showcase Brighton Rock, a rip-roaring version of the then new Bohemian Rhapsody and the crowd-pleasing Rock 'n' Roll Medley, this hour-long concert shows Queen at an early peak and poised to conquer the world.

programme.title: Freddie Mercury: The Final Act
programme.desc: The story of the extraordinary final chapter of Freddie Mercury’s life and how, after his death from Aids, Queen staged one of the biggest concerts in history, the Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert at Wembley Stadium, to celebrate his life and challenge the prejudices around HIV/Aids. The film hears from those who performed at the epic gig, including Gary Cherone (Extreme), Roger Daltrey (The Who), Joe Elliott (Def Leppard), Lisa Stansfield and Paul Young, as well as the concert’s promoter, Harvey Goldsmith. For the first time, Freddie's story is told alongside the experiences of those who tested positive for HIV and lost loved ones during the same period. Medical practitioners, survivors and human rights campaigners, including Peter Tatchell, recount the intensity of living through the Aids pandemic and the moral panic it brought about.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: Freddie Mercury’s image is known around the world. He was one of the most photographed men in history. But could just a handful of photos uncover new truths about someone we think we all know? This documentary throws a unique lens onto an extraordinary life, focusing on ten defining pictures – from iconic shots to private snaps – with their secrets revealed by those who were there and those who knew Freddie Mercury best.

programme.title: Evil Does Not Exist
programme.desc: The lives of a man and his neighbours are disrupted when a camping development is planned in their idyllic town in the Japanese countryside. In Japanese with English subtitles.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The Countryfile photographic competition comes to WWT Slimbridge in Gloucestershire, where John Craven and Charlotte Smith are joined by zoologist, presenter and author Megan McCubbin to choose 12 images capturing the signs of the seasons for the 2027 Countryfile Calendar, raising money for BBC Children in Need. The team also explore the reserve as summer gives way to autumn, encountering one of its rarest residents, the common crane, and discovering how the wetlands are prepared for the season ahead. Away from Slimbridge, Charlotte investigates the impact of drought on farming and asks the prime minister whether the government is doing enough to support those affected.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: In three of Derek’s top coastal rambles, he gets a dunking in Pembrokeshire, discovers why Porth Neigwl is dubbed Hell’s Mouth and meets some volunteers called the Silver Slashers.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: With the days getting shorter, and the nights cooler, George Anderson and Calum Clunie review some of the Beechgrove planting projects they started in the spring. A new addition was Calum’s family plot, based on the standard garden size of a new build property, and Calum returns to harvest and assess just how productive the area has been. George and Calum are in the trials bed to compare how the various club root-resistant varieties of brassica have performed after the infection was found in this area of the garden. The pair also visit the grass garden that was completely overhauled and replanted at the start of the series. There are visits to Jenna McDonald at her allotment in Perth and Colin Crosbie’s plot just outside Dumfries, and there are all the usual weekly handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt serves up a tasty menu of treats by favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Paul Ainsworth serves up a croque madame with a Cornish cheddar rarebit, Marmite butter and a crispy fried egg. Ching-He Huang fires up the wok for her sweet and sticky pineapple chicken with fragrant guo bao rice. Jeremy Lee prepares his roast pork with bitter leaves for Hollywood superstar Stanley Tucci, while Max La Manna makes the most of one of the UK’s most wasted ingredients – potatoes. Poppy O’Toole serves up a two-course potato meal using just two pots, and Mo Gilligan tucks into either his food heaven, curry goat, or his food hell, panettone pudding. Meanwhile, Rick Stein uncovers the secrets behind the iconic Carmarthen ham, and the Hairy Bikers rustle up a classic Corsican dish.

programme.title: Caribbean Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Levi Roots spices up ocean-fresh mackerel on a Cornish beach, challenges loyal Cornish pasty eaters in Falmouth to try his golden vegetable patties and visits Bristol to taste a Caribbean twist on British favourite steak and chips.

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Cooking
programme.desc: Nigel pairs spice with contrasting cooling flavours as he makes a chicken and chilli curry, spiced rice pudding and hot and spicy prawns.

programme.title: The Mirror Crack'd
programme.desc: The quiet English village of St Mary Mead is disrupted when a Hollywood film crew introduce inflated egos and cold-blooded murder. Miss Marple, of course, investigates.

programme.title: Equestrian: Burghley Horse Trials
programme.desc: Coverage from the 2026 Burghley Horse Trials.

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: The four remaining pairs face their biggest challenge yet in a deal that straddles Berlin and London, two of the world’s leading art destinations. Who can make it through to the semi-final? Back working in teams, one half travel to the German capital of Berlin with series mentor Cordelia de Freitas, where they must do deals with trailblazing international artists. The other half remain in London with Steph and guest mentor Ani Petrov, marketing and data analytics expert at Artsy. Together, they try to create a buzz around their chosen artists and drive potential buyers to a global online auction of their work.

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Two women lost in time: an enigmatic Indian woman and an 18th-century Scottish artist. Will this quest uncover a double attribution leading to a six-figure price tag?

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: From the urban rhythms of Bernstein's West Side Story and On the Town to Gershwin's jazz-infused Rhapsody in Blue and the wide-open landscapes of Copland’s Appalachian Spring and Moross’s The Big Country, Marin Alsop conducts this barnstorming celebration of music from her homeland. The Marcus Roberts Trio are special guests alongside the Philharmonia. Katie Derham presents.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: It's day five, and the pilgrims prepare for the challenging Alpine paths ahead of them. As they go along the path, they discover part of their route is covered by a deep snow drift, see how the people of St Anton harness the power of mountain water to make their own electricity, and reach the highest point of their Camino.

programme.title: Rob and Rylan's Passage to India
programme.desc: The boys board a packed train to Rajasthan during Diwali, the vibrant festival of lights. Known as the 'land of kings', Rajasthan enchants the pair with its grand forts and opulent palaces. But they also discover the skilled craftsmanship of the cities of Udaipur and Jaipur, from ornate block printing to dazzling traditional jewellery. They try miniature painting, hear a worrying prediction from an astrologer and celebrate Diwali with the crown prince of Jaipur.

programme.title: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
programme.desc: Classic western adventure, starring Paul Newman and Robert Redford as legendary outlaws Butch and Kid.

programme.title: Golf: Walker Cup
programme.desc: The best amateur golfers in the world contest the 51st Walker Cup as Great Britain and Ireland take on the United States at Lahinch in County Clare, Ireland. Great Britain and Ireland are looking to win back the trophy on home soil, with the USA having won the last five contests. Recent winner of the US Amateur Jack Whaley stars for the hosts in an event that has an illustrious list of previous participants, including Jack Nicklaus, Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy, Scottie Scheffler and Justin Rose.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: The Newbiggin crew race to the rescue of three children who have been swept out to sea on a small inflatable dinghy; the situation escalates when reports come in that the father has attempted to swim out to try to rescue them himself. In Selsey, a mayday comes in from a vessel taking on water in the English Channel; one of the casualties is reported to have suffered a head injury. On the Dorset coast, the Lyme Regis crew respond to reports of a couple cut off by a landslide on a notorious stretch of coast. And reports of two kite surfers struggling in the water put the Shoreham crew on red alert.

programme.title: This is CBBC!
programme.desc: Tune every day from 7.00am.

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Children's animation. Set on a remote rural farm, Shaun's flock lives a peaceful life under the watchful eye of their sheepdog Bitzer. It is a scorching hot day and the flock are desperate to cool down in the sheep dip, but there is one thing in their way.

programme.title: Danger Mouse
